name: Aquatic Thermoregulation Blubber Layer
target_system: integumentary/metabolic (subcutaneous fat insulation for aquatic environments)
description: Induces growth of a specialized subcutaneous fat layer with the insulating properties of marine mammal blubber, specifically designed for extended cold-water immersion. The blubber layer is 1–2 cm thick over the torso and thighs, providing thermal insulation that allows comfortable immersion in water down to 4°C for extended periods. Combined with the gill modification and deep-pressure resistance, it creates a comprehensive aquatic adaptation suite. The blubber layer adds 8–12 kg of body mass and is visible — the user has a distinctly rounded, smooth body contour that reads as robustly healthy rather than obese. In Old Harbor, where underwater work is constant and the harbor water is cold year-round, the modification is standard equipment for divers and maritime workers.
source_organism: Phoca vitulina (harbor seal), Mirounga leonina (southern elephant seal, deep-water insulation variant)
procedure: Systemic retroviral injection targeting subcutaneous fat cell conversion, 3 sessions over 4 weeks
reversibility: Partially reversible with fat cell reconversion; some thickness persists
side_effects: Overheating in warm environments or during exercise
Buoyancy dramatically increased — excellent for swimming, complicated for diving
Body shape changes may require new wardrobe
Blubber layer makes subcutaneous injections difficult — needles must be longer
social_perception: Practical and aquatic-culture specific. In Old Harbor, Seal Skin is unremarkable — everyone who works the water has it. On land and in other districts, the distinctive body shape identifies the user as a maritime worker.
story_hooks: A Seal Skin diver's blubber layer begins absorbing environmental pollutants from contaminated harbor water — their body is accumulating toxins at a rate that will become lethal, and they're not the only one
An insurance company denies a cold-water drowning claim because the victim had Seal Skin — they should have survived the water temperature, meaning something else killed them
